title: Multi-tenant KV snapshot compaction and warmup admission control
creator: Ayesha Patel
description:
Problem: Multi-tenant workloads show poor tail latency during bursts because cold KV slots are restored synchronously during prefill, causing decode stalls and noisy neighbor eviction. Current eviction is LRU-biased but lacks a way to compact fragmented microblocks or to snapshot a tenant's working set for fast warmup. We need a robust approach to: (1) reduce stalling during prefill, (2) avoid repeated expensive restores for tenants with intermittent traffic, and (3) ensure fairness across tenants without excessive memory churn.

Goal: Implement a snapshot-based compaction and admission-control system that: snapshot-quilts low-entropy fragments into compact warmup bundles, maintains a small tenant-level "ghost pool" metadata layer for quick reclaim/restore decisions, and adds an admission-control policy for prefill that hedges warmup restores to avoid decode waves.

Outcomes: Reduced 99th decode latency for bursty tenants by >= 25%, lower restore I/O during hot switches by >= 40%, and measurable decrease in cross-tenant eviction churn.

Links: Confluence design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INFR/KV+Snapshot+Compaction+Design, RFC: https://go.redwood.ai/rfcs/kv-snapshot-compaction, prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving/pull/9876, dashboard: https://dashboards.redwood.ai/d/paged-attn/kv-warmup-telemetry

Notes: This ticket focuses on runtime + allocator changes; it intentionally avoids storage format rewrites and defers long-term on-disk delta formats to a follow-up (see followups).
acceptance_criteria: Snapshot compaction produces warmup bundles < 512KB on average for tenant working sets under 1M tokens
Prefill admission control reduces synchronous restore calls per burst by >= 40% in load tests
End-to-end e2e benchmark shows 99th decode latency improvement >= 25% on representative multi-tenant traces
No regressions in memory correctness or data corruption; all unit/integration tests pass and chaos tests show stability
design_decisions: Use lightweight immutable snapshots (read-only bundles) to avoid coordination during reads; snapshots are built by a background compactor
Maintain a small per-tenant ghost-pool index (metadata only) so eviction can demote entries to ghost rather than fully discard, enabling cheaper rehydrate heuristics

Admission control will use a three-state prefill hedging: immediate restore (latency-critical), hedged restore (start background restore and serve degraded decode if possible), and deferred restore (prefetch asynchronously)
Compaction window set to 30s by default with tunable burst-amplification factor; can be disabled for dedicated tenants
tradeoffs: Snapshot bundles increase background CPU and temporary memory during compaction, but reduce synchronous restore I/O and tail latencies
Ghost-pool increases metadata overhead (~2-4% memory) but reduces full evictions and repeated full restores
Admission control may slightly increase average latency for non-critical tokens when hedging is enabled, in exchange for better tail behavior during bursts
rollout_plan: Feature flag behind runtime flag 'kv_snapshot_compaction' scoped to canary tenants
Phase 1 (canary): Enable background compactor + ghost-pool metadata for 5% of traffic, collect metrics for 2 weeks
Phase 2 (staged): Enable hedged prefill admission control and tune thresholds via load tests in staging
Phase 3 (ramp): Expand to 30% then 100% after verifying metrics and resolving regressions
Fallback: runtime flag off reverts to prior LRU eviction and synchronous restore behavior
metrics: compactor.cpu_seconds and compactor.temp_mem_peak - to monitor resource cost
ghostpool.hits and ghostpool.promote_rate - to validate effectiveness
test_plan: Unit tests for snapshot bundle serializer/deserializer and ghost-pool metadata transitions
Integration test with synthetic multi-tenant trace exercising burst patterns (3x baseline qps bursts)
Chaos test: random tenant churn + forced compaction pauses to verify graceful fallback
Performance load test against hardware matrix (A100, H100, and CPU-only fallback) to measure resource tradeoffs
Canary smoke validation using dashboard alerts and automated rollback if 99th latency regresses > 10%
